claim: Blindness affects 45 million people around the world with an increase of 1 to 2 million people each year.
source: Blindness affects 45 million people around the world with an increase of 1 to 2 million people each year (Resnikoff et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Resnikoff et al., 2004

claim: The two main retinal pathologies are age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP).
source: The two main retinal pathologies are age-related macular degeneration (AMD, Ambati and Fowler, 2012; Finger et al., 2011) and Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP, Bocquet et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple sources on AMD and RP

claim: Retinal degeneration inexorably leads to blindness.
source: retinal degeneration inexorably leads to blindness (Tsujikawa et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsujikawa et al., 2008

claim: Retinal prostheses provide a promising solution that remains to date a unique alternative for patients with retinal degeneration.
source: In this perspective, retinal prostheses provide a promising solution that remains to date a unique alternative for the patients.
evidence: Based on the context of irreversible retinal degeneration and lack of other treatments

claim: Restoring some visual perception using implants has been already achieved.
source: Restoring some visual perception using implants has been already achieved (Humayun et al., 2012; Shepherd et al., 2013; Zrenner et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple clinical studies

claim: Current retinal prostheses still offer insufficient gains in visual acuity.
source: but still offers insufficient gains in visual acuity (Humayun et al., 2012; Zrenner et al., 2010); (Nanduri et al., 2012; Rizzo, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple clinical studies

claim: The Argus II epiretinal prosthesis and the subretinal alpha IMS microphotodiode array restore some visual function although with spatial resolution that does not allow for the recognition of faces or autonomous locomotion.
source: Despite having fundamentally different designs and operating modes, the two main models of prostheses proposed to the patients with RP (Argus II epiretinal prosthesis and the subretinal alpha IMS microphotodiode array) restore some visual function although with a spatial resolution (Ahuja and Behrend, 2013; Humayun et al., 2012); (Stingl et al., 2013) that does not allow for the recognition of faces or autonomous locomotion.
evidence: Supported by citations to clinical studies on these specific devices

claim: The cochlear implant field has demonstrated the importance of developing animal models for better understanding of the underlying physiological processes.
source: This latter field, well in advance compared to retinal implants, has already demonstrated the importance of developing animal models for better understanding of the underlying physiological processes (Fallon and Shepherd, 2009; Miller et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to cochlear implant research

claim: Most pioneering animal studies were not designed to characterize and calibrate the functional activation of the visual system.
source: However, most were not designed to characterize and calibrate the functional activation of the visual system (Chowdhury et al., 2008; Eger et al., 2005; Mandel et al., 2013; Nadig, 1999; Schanze et al., 2003; Walter et al., 2005; Wong et al., 2009)
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple animal studies

claim: Most pioneering animal studies did not probe the functional impact of implants through systematic comparison with visual activation.
source: nor probed the functional impact of implants through systematic comparison with visual activation (Chowdhury et al., 2008; Cicione et al., 2012; Eger et al., 2005; Fransen et al., 2014; Mandel et al., 2013; Matteucci et al., 2013; Schanze et al., 2003; Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple animal studies

claim: The study developed an acute animal model to quantitatively assess the functional impact of retinal prostheses by comparing the downstream activation of the visual system in response to visual versus artificial stimuli.
source: To address this issue, we developed an acute animal model to quantitatively assess the functional impact of retinal prostheses by comparing the downstream activation of the visual system in response to visual versus artificial stimuli, using intrinsic optical imaging of the primary visual cortex (V1).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used in the study

claim: Gias and colleagues have provided a retinotopic description of the rat visual cortex using optical imaging.
source: So far only Gias and colleagues (Gias et al., 2004) have provided a retinotopic description of the rat visual cortex using optical imaging.
evidence: Supported by citation to Gias et al., 2004

claim: Prosthetic stimulation generates a functional activation that occurs at the expected retinotopic location and amplitude.
source: Using this cartographic benchmark, we demonstrate that prosthetic stimulation generates a functional activation that occurs at the expected retinotopic location and amplitude.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study based on experimental data

claim: The aspect ratio and the extent of the activation from prosthetic stimulation are significantly larger than expected.
source: However, the aspect ratio and the extent of the activation are significantly larger than expected.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study based on experimental data

claim: The distorted activation profile can be accounted for by the existence of two sources of diffusion: passive diffusion and activation of ganglion cells' axons en passant.
source: This can be explained through a simple model with two sources of diffusion: an electrical passive diffusion and the activation of axons en passant from ganglion cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on modeling of the experimental observations

claim: Reverse-engineered electrical pulses based on impedance spectroscopy decreases the extent and aspect-ratio of cortical activation.
source: Reverse-engineered electrical pulses based on impedance spectroscopy is the only solution we tested that decreases the extent and aspect-ratio, providing a promising solution for clinical applications.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study based on experimental data

claim: The experimental protocol was approved by the local Ethical Committee for Animal Research.
source: The experimental protocol was approved beforehand by the local Ethical Committee for Animal Research and all procedures complied with the French and European regulations on Animal Research (approval n°A12/01/13) as well as the guidelines from the Society for Neuroscience.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval

claim: A total of 35 Brown Norway male rats were used in the study.
source: A total of 35 Brown Norway male rats (1.5–3 months old, 230–320 g) were anesthetized using an intraperitoneal injection of urethane.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects

claim: The bone over V1 was thinned with a drill until a clear optical access to V1 surface was obtained instead of performing a complete craniotomy.
source: Instead of a complete craniotomy, the bone was thinned with a drill until a clear optical access to V1 surface was obtained.
evidence: This is a description of the surgical procedure

claim: The MEAs were implanted between the pigmentary epithelium and the outer segment photoreceptor layer.
source: The MEAs were implanted between the pigmentary epithelium and the outer segment photoreceptor layer (Figure 1C bottom row).
evidence: This is a description of the implantation procedure with reference to Figure 1C

claim: The cortical retinotopic magnification factor is 22 µm/° in the rat.
source: We observed a linear increase of cortical distance with visual distance, at a rate of 22 µm/° (in accordance with the literature) (Gias et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a measurement from the study that is consistent with prior literature

claim: For visual stimuli, the average cortical positional error was 0.32 ± 0.22 mm.
source: On average, the cortical error was 0.32 ± 0.22 mm for visual stimuli, 72% of the data points falling within the retinotopic representation of the 20° stimulus (<0.44 mm).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: For single electrode stimulation, the positional error was 0.46 ± 0.27 mm.
source: For SE, the estimation of the position of the evoked activity was quite accurate (error of 0.46 ± 0.27 mm), 55% of evoked responses falling within the retinotopic expected position.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: For whole MEA stimulation, the positional error was 0.68 ± 0.47 mm.
source: Finally, wMEA activations yielded responses with more variable and less accurate position than SE with an average error of 0.68 ± 0.47 mm, 38% of the evoked positions being within the expected representation.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: The extent of cortical activation linearly increased with visual stimulus size with an average slope of 81 µm/°.
source: As shown in the example of Figure 3A, the extent of cortical activation linearly increased with visual stimulus size with an average slope of 81 µm/° when estimated at population level (Figure 3B, N = 7).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with reference to figures

claim: The active surface diameters of the SE and wMEA were 0.05 and 0.65 mm, equivalent to 1 and 11° of visual angle.
source: In comparison, the active surface diameters of the SE and wMEA were of 0.05 and 0.65 mm (see Materials and methods) equivalent to 1 and 11° of visual angle (Hughes, 1979), respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement of the electrode dimensions with citation for conversion to visual angle

claim: wMEA stimulation led to a systematic and highly significant increase of the cortical activation extent in 94% of the cases (17/18 conditions, 10 animals).
source: we observed a systematic and highly significant increase of the cortical activation extent induced by wMEA stimulation in 94% of the cases (17/18 conditions, 10 animals; see Materials and methods and Figure 3D legend for details on statistical procedures)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: wMEA stimulation led to an average increase of 2.9 ± 2.01 times the activation extent of the visual stimulation.
source: with an average increase of 2.9 ± 2.01 times the activation extent of the visual stimulation (Figure 3D, thin gray lines).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: SE stimulation led to an average activation size of 0.9 ± 0.5 times their 20° visual counterparts.
source: In comparison, SE stimulation led to an average activation size of 0.9 ± 0.5 times their 20° visual counterparts (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: The equivalent visual stimulus sizes that would have evoked such cortical activations reached on average 24.4 ± 10.6 and 32.2 ± 11.5° for SE and wMEA configurations, respectively.
source: These values reached on average 24.4 ± 10.6 and 32.2 ± 11.5° instead of 1 and 11° for the SE and wMEA configurations, respectively.
evidence: This is a calculated value based on the visual-size tuning function

claim: An inter-electrode spacing of at least 0.8 to 1.2 mm on the retina would be required to yield non-overlapping cortical activations at low- and high-intensity respectively.
source: Our results unambiguously demonstrate that prosthetic retinal stimulation generates too large activation to obtain the necessary independence between electrodes; an inter-electrode spacing of at least 0.8 to 1.2 mm on the retina, at low- and high-intensity respectively, would be required to yield non-overlapping cortical activations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data

claim: SE stimulation showed a highly significant increase in the aspect ratio of the evoked activations compared to their visual counterparts (1.66 ± 0.43 vs. 1.35 ± 0.19).
source: Using pairwise visual-prosthetic comparison, we found a highly significant (see Figure 4B legend) increase in the aspect ratio of the evoked activations for SE condition compared to their visual counterparts (1.66 ± 0.43 vs. 1.35 ± 0.19)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: wMEA stimulation showed no significant increase in aspect ratio compared to visual counterparts.
source: but none for wMEA.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: The elongations in cortical activation could be caused by the recruitment of ganglion cells' axons en passant leading to oriented anisotropic cortical activations.
source: These elongations could be caused by the recruitment of ganglion cells' axons en passant leading to oriented anisotropic cortical activations (Figure 1A right).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the observed data

claim: The observed orientations of cortical activation deviated from an optimal radial organization to the cortical position representing the optic disk by only 13.3° (median value across N = 20 activations).
source: Observed orientations of cortical activation deviated from an optimal radial organization (dashed lines) to this cortical position by only 13.3° (median value across N = 20 activations).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: The observed angular deviation of 13.3° is significantly smaller than what would be expected by chance (p=0.02).
source: Our observation of 13.3° (red line) is significantly smaller than what would be expected by chance (p=0.02, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a statistical result comparing observed data to a null distribution

claim: Center-of-masses of elongated activations all deviated away from the optic disk with an averaged angular deviation of −168°.
source: Center-of-masses all deviated away from the optic disk with an averaged angular deviation of −168° (opposite deviation being 180°).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: Increasing luminance non-linearly increased the cortical activation size and amplitude.
source: Increasing luminance non-linearly increased the cortical activation size and amplitude (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data

claim: The luminance of semi-saturation was 9.6 ± 2.9 cd/m2 for visual stimulation.
source: The luminance of semi-saturation was 9.6 ± 2.9 cd/m2.
evidence: This is a parameter from the Naka-Rushton fit to the experimental data

claim: The intensity of semi-saturation was significantly lower for SE than for wMEA (20.29 ± 3.25 µA vs. 52.66 ± 17.35 µA).
source: The intensity of semi-saturation (Figure 5F) was significantly lower for SE than for wMEA (20.29 ± 3.25 µA vs. 52.66 ± 17.35 µA, see legend for details on statistical procedure).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of parameters from fits to the experimental data

claim: Steep transitions were observed for wMEA (n = 5.58 ± 3.54) and for visual luminance (n = 6.05 ± 3.01) whereas more gradual transitions were observed for SE (n = 1.34 ± 0.6).
source: Steep transitions were observed for wMEA (n = 5.58 ± 3.54) and for visual luminance (n = 6.05 ± 3.01) whereas more gradual transitions were observed for SE (n = 1.34 ± 0.6) which significantly differed from wMEA and visual stimuli (see Figure 5G legend).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of parameters from fits to the experimental data

claim: The operating range of the intensity response function in visual stimulation was on average 9.2 ± 4.8 cd/m2.
source: As a consequence, the operating range (see Materials and methods) of the intensity response function in visual stimulation was on average 9.2 ± 4.8 cd/m2
evidence: This is a calculated value from the experimental data

claim: The operating range for wMEA was 82.5 ± 88.4 µA.
source: 82.5 ± 88.4 µA for wMEA
evidence: This is a calculated value from the experimental data

claim: The operating range for SE was 182.6 ± 151.4 µA.
source: and much broader for SE (182.6 ± 151.4 µA).
evidence: This is a calculated value from the experimental data

claim: The polarity of symmetric biphasic pulses did not significantly influence the extent of the cortical activation for the two intensity levels tested.
source: In the example shown and over the population (Figure 6A–B), our results showed that the polarity of symmetric biphasic pulses did not significantly influence the extent of the cortical activation for the two intensity levels tested.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: The polarity was found to have a significant effect in asymmetric pulses delivered at 200 µA.
source: However, the polarity was found to have a significant effect in asymmetric pulses delivered at 200 µA (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: The combination of asymmetric with anodic-first stimulation generated smaller activation of 1.66 ± 0.71 mm corresponding to 17.12 ± 8.11°eq (N = 7).
source: The combination of asymmetric with anodic-first stimulation (Figure 6C top right) generated smaller activation of 1.66 ± 0.71 mm corresponding to 17.12 ± 8.11°eq (N = 7), smaller than the three other combinations.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: The reduction in activation size with asymmetric anodic-first stimulation was not systematic (70% of the cases compared to the symmetrical pulse) and small (20.43% ± 54.32).
source: However, this reduction was not systematic (70% of the cases compared to the symmetrical pulse) and small (20.43% ± 54.32, the corresponding [20-50-80] percentiles being [34.78–32.93–63.89]%).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the experimental data

claim: The impedance phase and magnitude of the electrode-retina interface was found to be highly capacitive, yielding strong distortion of the applied stimulus.
source: In a previous study (Pham et al., 2013), we indeed showed that the impedance phase and magnitude of the electrode-retina interface was found to be highly capacitive, yielding strong distortion of the applied stimulus (Figure 7A, left bottom) and lateral diffusion of the injected pattern.
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors, cited and referenced

claim: For 100% and 88% of the low and high voltage level cases respectively, the adapted pattern injected through SE decreased the extent of the activation.
source: For 100% and 88% of the low and high voltage level cases respectively (5 Vpp and 12 Vpp, Vpp: Volts peak-to-peak), the adapted pattern injected through SE decreased the extent of the activation (Figure 7B top maps & 7C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: The significant decrease in activation extent with IS-adapted pulses varied on average from 36 ± 32% to 20.7 ± 29.2% at low and high voltage, respectively.
source: This significant decrease (see Figure 7C legend) varied on average from 36 ± 32% to 20.7 ± 29.2% at low and high voltage, respectively (the corresponding [20-50-80] percentiles were [11.78–27.50–59.05] and [1.89–6.56–39.67]%).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data

claim: At high voltage, the reduction in extent with IS-adapted pulses was not accompanied by a significant change in response amplitude.
source: Importantly, at high voltage it was not accompanied by a significant change in response amplitude (Wilcoxon rank sum test: p=0.546, n = 8, N = 4)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data

claim: The recording of robust and reliable electrically and visually evoked responses indicates that both types of information are efficiently transmitted to the primary visual cortex.
source: The recording of robust and reliable electrically and visually evoked responses indicates that both types of information are efficiently transmitted to the primary visual cortex and prove the functional integrity of the retinal tissue after implantation, which was also anatomically confirmed by retinal imaging (OCT).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations

claim: Population activation of the first cortical integration stage is correlated to underlying evoked percepts.
source: The working hypothesis of this study is that population activation of the first cortical integration stage is correlated to underlying evoked percepts, as suggested by many studies (Chen et al., 2006; Ni, 2010; Palmer et al., 2007; Tehovnik and Slocum, 2006).
evidence: This is a working hypothesis supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: The link between population activation in optical imaging and spiking discharge has long been established.
source: Furthermore, the link between population activation in optical imaging and spiking discharge has long been established (Chen et al., 2012; Das and Gilbert, 1995; Shmuel and Grinvald, 1996; Toth et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: The spatial profile of cortical population activation in the awake monkey biases the shape of the evoked percept.
source: Lastly, a recent study showed that the spatial profile of cortical population activation in the awake monkey biases the shape of the evoked percept (Michel et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Michel et al., 2013

claim: The degree of positional precision was higher in SE compared to wMEA.
source: The degree of positional precision, higher in SE compared to wMEA, was of the same order of magnitude as the 20° visual stimuli.
evidence: This is a comparison of results from the experimental data

claim: Increasing the level of current intensity increases the amplitude of the evoked cortical response with a sigmoidal profile similar to the one observed with visual luminance.
source: We have also shown that increasing the level of current intensity increases the amplitude of the evoked cortical response with a sigmoidal profile similar to the one observed with visual luminance.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the experimental data

claim: SE offers a larger operating range (182 vs. 82 µA for wMEA) to cover a theoretical modulation range of about 50 cd/m2.
source: However, our experiments unveiled that SE offers a larger operating range (182 vs. 82 µA for wMEA) to cover a theoretical modulation range of about 50 cd/m2.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the experimental data

claim: Small electrode sizes will be more appropriate to make fine manipulation of stimulus intensity.
source: This result demonstrates that small electrode sizes will be more appropriate to make fine manipulation of stimulus intensity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data

claim: Increasing stimulus intensity increases both the response size and the response amplitude.
source: Importantly, our results also revealed that the increasing stimulus intensity increases both the response size and the response amplitude.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data

claim: The size elicited with standard parameters is approximately 2.4 to 5.8 times larger than expected for wMEA and SE, respectively.
source: Our results demonstrate that the size elicited with standard parameters is approximately 2.4 to 5.8 times larger than expected for wMEA and SE, respectively.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the experimental data

claim: The spatial resolution of the prosthetic retinal activation measured in the experiments is about a millimeter of retinal space.
source: The spatial resolution of the prosthetic retinal activation measured in our experiments, about a millimeter of retinal space, is actually comparable to what has been reported in other animals (as estimated from Eger et al., 2005; Schanze et al., 2003) as well as in human studies (as estimated from Ahuja and Behrend, 2013; Humayun et al., 2012; Stingl et al., 2013) and extends beyond the retinal point spread function (Stett et al., 2000, 2007).
evidence: This is a measurement from the study compared to literature values

claim: Anesthetized mice have less surround inhibition than when awake.
source: Indeed, recent experiments showed that anesthetized mice have less surround inhibition than when awake (Vaiceliunaite et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vaiceliunaite et al., 2013

claim: Anesthesia affects not simply the inhibition but more probably the balance between excitation and inhibition.
source: However, Vizuete et al (Vizuete et al., 2012) have shown that anesthesia affects not simply the inhibition but more probably the balance between excitation and inhibition (see also Chemla and Chavane (2016)).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vizuete et al., 2012 and Chemla and Chavane, 2016

claim: Fransen et al. discard the possibility of direct RGCs activation through near infrared laser stimulation of photovoltaic subretinal array because of the absence of responses in the superior colliculus using inner retina synaptic blockers.
source: In contrast, Fransen et al. (Fransen et al., 2014) discard the possibility of direct RGCs activation through near infrared laser stimulation of photovoltaic subretinal array because of the absence of responses in the superior colliculus using inner retina synaptic blockers.
evidence: Supported by citation to Fransen et al., 2014

claim: The model predicts that to account for the observed spatial profiles, axons en passant should contribute to the same proportion than direct activation of the retina.
source: Our model also allowed predicting that, to account for the observed spatial profiles, axons en passant should contribute to the same proportion than direct activation of the retina.
evidence: This is a prediction from the computational model based on fitting to experimental data

claim: Charge balanced biphasic pulses, delivered in voltage or current mode injection, are of common use in human and animal studies of prosthetic vision.
source: Charge balanced biphasic pulses, delivered in voltage or current mode injection, are of common use in human (Ahuja and Behrend, 2013; Fujikado et al., 2007; Humayun et al., 2012; Klauke et al., 2011; Nanduri et al., 2012; Rizzo, 2003; Shepherd et al., 2013; Stingl et al., 2013; Wilke et al., 2011; Zrenner, 2013; Zrenner et al., 2010) or animal (Chowdhury et al., 2008; Cicione et al., 2012; Eckhorn et al., 2006; Eger et al., 2005; Elfar et al., 2009; Matteucci et al., 2013; Nadig, 1999; Schanze et al., 2003; Walter et al., 2005; Wong et al., 2009) studies of prosthetic vision.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple human and animal studies

claim: There is a large consensus concerning the use of cathodic pulse first for epiretinal stimulation.
source: In the literature, we observed a large consensus concerning the use of cathodic pulse first for epiretinal stimulation (Ahuja and Behrend, 2013; Eckhorn et al., 2006; Eger et al., 2005; Elfar et al., 2009; Fried et al., 2006; Nanduri et al., 2012; Schanze et al., 2003; Walter et al., 2005) although not for subretinal, suprachoroidal and extraocular approaches (Chowdhury et al., 2008; Cicione et al., 2012; Eckhorn et al., 2006; Fujikado et al., 2007; Matteucci et al., 2013; Stingl et al., 2013; Wilke et al., 2011; Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: The use of single cathodic pulse lowers the threshold of retinal ganglion cells, lowers the latency of inner retina mediated RGCs response and targets more specifically RGCs cell bodies when compared to anodal pulses.
source: It has been shown in vitro (Jensen et al., 2005) that the use of single cathodic pulse lowers the threshold of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), lowers the latency of inner retina mediated RGCs response and targets more specifically RGCs cell bodies when compared to anodal pulses.
evidence: Supported by citation to Jensen et al., 2005

claim: Chowdhury et al. did not find any significant effect of the pulse polarity on the threshold of V1 electrically evoked potentials using an extraocular device.
source: Using an extraocular device, Chowdhury et al. did not find any significant effect of the pulse polarity on the threshold of V1 electrically evoked potentials.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Chowdhury et al., 2008

claim: The result that anodic asymmetric pulses were the best among classical stimulations to restrict cortical activations contradicts the prediction of the pioneer modeling work of McIntyre & Grill.
source: This result contradicts the prediction of the pioneer modeling work of McIntyre & Grill (McIntyre and Grill, 2000), which predicts more focal activation for cathodic asymmetrical pulses using a cable model.
evidence: This is a comparison of the study's findings to predictions from a cited modeling study

claim: Current steering methods could improve the spatial resolution of the implant up to the activation of a single RGC type with a single action potential resolution.
source: These authors showed in in-vitro isolated retinal preparation, that it was possible to improve the spatial resolution of the implant up to the activation of a single RGC type with a single action potential resolution (Jepson et al., 2013; Sekirnjak et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jepson et al., 2013 and Sekirnjak et al., 2008

claim: Electrical stimulation adaptation systematically and accurately decreased the activation spread while preserving their location and amplitude, when compared to their paired controls.
source: Our results show that electrical stimulation adaptation systematically and accurately decreased the activation spread while preserving their location and amplitude, when compared to their paired controls.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the experimental data

claim: IS-adapted stimulation was the only configuration tested whose decrease in extent was not accompanied by an increase in aspect ratio, similarly to functional visual stimulation.
source: Crucially, it was the only configuration we tested whose decrease in extent was not accompanied by an increase in aspect ratio (Figure 8, filled circles), similarly to functional visual stimulation.
evidence: This is a comparison of results across different experimental conditions

claim: IS-adapted stimulation reduces both the electrical diffusion extent and the axons en passant activation.
source: This strongly suggests that such stimulation reduces both the electrical diffusion extent (although not completely) and the axons en passant activation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results

claim: The duration of each adapted pulse in the tissue is much longer (1.2 ms on average) than the transients contained in the non-adapted pulses (0.2 ms on average).
source: A second mechanism would originate from the fact that the duration of each adapted pulse (anodic or cathodic) in the tissue is much longer (1.2 ms on average) than the transients contained in the non-adapted pulses (0.2 ms on average).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental data

claim: Axons have shorter chronaxie, generally some hundreds of microseconds, than cell bodies, generally several milliseconds.
source: This can favor activation of cell bodies since axons have shorter chronaxie, generally some hundreds of microseconds, than cell bodies, generally several milliseconds (McIntyre and Grill, 2002; Nowak and Bullier, 1998b, 1998a; Ranck, 1975; Stern et al., 2015; Tehovnik and Slocum, 2009, Histed et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies on chronaxie

claim: Supervised adaptation of electrical pulse based on the electrical properties of the electrode-tissue interface is a promising solution for retinal, cochlear prosthetic stimulations and more generally for all neuro-stimulation applications.
source: Supervised adaptation of electrical pulse based on the electrical properties of the electrode-tissue interface is therefore a promising solution for retinal, but also probably, for cochlear prosthetic stimulations and more generally for all neuro-stimulation applications.
evidence: This is a conclusion and speculation based on the study's findings

claim: Z-score and DI/I measures were highly and significantly correlated (median correlation coefficient r2 = 0.81).
source: Note that Z-score and DI/I measures were highly and significantly correlated (median correlation coefficient r2 = 0.81 between all pixels of Z-score vs. DI/I maps with the corresponding [20-50-80] percentiles being [0.73--0.81--0.88]%, all pval = 1.40e−45, N = 9 rats, n = 225 maps).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the relationship between two measurement methods

claim: The MEAs used were planar MEAs of 1 and 1.2 mm diameter comprising respectively 9 and 17 platinum contacts.
source: These planar MEAs of 1 and 1.2 mm diameter comprise respectively 9 and 17 (50 μm radius, 3 μm thick) platinum (Pt) contacts and a large annular Pt counter-electrode (CE) within a polyimide flexible substrate (Figure 1C top row).
evidence: This is a description of the materials used in the study

claim: The OCT has an axial resolution of 5 μm.
source: The OCT has an axial resolution of 5 μm.
evidence: This is a specification of the imaging equipment used

claim: After each implantation a recovery period from 30 min to 1 hr was respected before starting data acquisition.
source: After each implantation a recovery period from 30 min to 1 hr was respected before starting data acquisition and the presence of visual evoked cortical activation was used to probe the functional integrity of the implanted retinal tissue.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol
